schoollink.name: SchoolLink
schoollink.summary: An attendance and parent-notification platform for secondary schools in Cameroon. Teachers record attendance per period on a phone, assistant discipline masters record lateness at the gate, and every absence reaches the guardian the same day. Repeated patterns raise risk alerts that a Discipline Master decides on. The rules never decide on their own.
schoollink.role: Sole developer: specification, architecture, backend, web dashboard, Android app and deployment.

scolarys.name: Scolarys
scolarys.summary: A school management system built during my academic internship at Collège Adventiste d'Odza in Yaoundé, replacing a legacy .NET desktop application. It covers enrolment, timetabling, mark entry, averages and ranking, discipline records, bilingual report cards, tuition in four instalments and a parent portal.
scolarys.role: Sole developer, and the requirements work before any code.
scolarys.constraint: Over 200 teachers share at most 5 desktop computers during mark-entry season.
scolarys.status: Delivered and defended on 1 October 2026. The code is private because it holds the institution's data.

1.title: Requirements before code
1.body: I ran the interviews with six Directeurs des Études and the Surveillant Général, then wrote the functional specification the build followed.

2.title: A domain model that fits the school
2.body: Francophone and anglophone sections plus a technical branch, modelled in 8 packages and about 107 classes, with sequential, termly and annual averages ranked by class and level.

3.title: Mark entry moved to the phone
3.body: A React Native app lets teachers enter marks on their own phones. It works offline once it has confirmed the entry session is open.

4.title: Payments and messages built in
4.body: Campay handles MTN and Orange Mobile Money for tuition, and SMS keeps parents informed. Report cards match the school's existing bilingual format.

aics.name: AICS Report Hub
aics.summary: A Django platform for managing final-year report submissions across multiple campuses. Campus admins register students and supervisors, supervisors issue one-time upload codes, students upload their PDF, and reports are publicly browsable, searchable and graded with feedback.

1.title: Four roles, scoped by campus
1.body: Role-based access on a custom user model, so each admin and supervisor only sees their own campus.

2.title: One-time upload codes
2.body: Supervisors issue a code per student, and the upload form validates it live before the file is sent.

3.title: PDFs served through the app
3.body: Reports are streamed by the application instead of being exposed as media files, and each upload gets an automatic first-page preview.

phone.label: Teacher's phone
phone.caption: Flutter, offline-first
phone.decision: Teacher screens are offline-first. The phone generates the record IDs and the API accepts idempotent PUT requests, so a phone coming back online can retry without creating duplicates.

api.label: REST API
api.caption: Spring Boot, JWT
api.decision: Every query is filtered by school and user scope on the server, taken from the JWT and never from the request. One modular monolith, 12 modules, one API.

db.label: Database
db.caption: PostgreSQL 16, Flyway
db.decision: An append-only audit log records every create, edit, cancel and export, and schema changes are versioned with Flyway.

outbox.label: Outbox
outbox.caption: Transactional table
outbox.decision: Notifications are written to a transactional outbox table in the same transaction as the absence, so a restart cannot lose one.

dispatcher.label: Dispatcher
dispatcher.caption: Firebase, SMS
dispatcher.decision: A separate dispatcher reads the outbox and retries failures. Guardians get a Firebase push, or a single SMS digest per day.

guardian.label: Guardian
guardian.caption: Informed the same day
guardian.decision: The guardian hears about an absence the same day. The system stores a birth year only, keeps no photos, and never puts phone numbers in URLs or logs.

privacy.intro: This site is the personal portfolio of {{name}}. This page explains what data is processed when you visit it, why, and how to exercise your rights.

body: {{name}}, Yaoundé, Cameroon. Contact: {{email}}.

2.title: Data collected
body: The site has no forms and creates no accounts.
Preferences saved in your browser (local storage, not cookies): your chosen language and your choice about audience measurement. This information never leaves your device.

Audience measurement, only if you accept it: Vercel Web Analytics and Vercel Speed Insights record pages viewed, the referring site, country, device type, browser and performance metrics. These tools use no cookies and cannot identify you personally.
Technical logs: like any host, Vercel processes your IP address and request details to serve the pages and keep the service secure.

3.title: Purposes and legal bases
body: Serving and protecting the site: legitimate interest.
Measuring audience and site speed to improve it: your consent, which you can withdraw at any time.

4.title: Contact by WhatsApp or e-mail
body: If you contact me by WhatsApp or e-mail, I use your details and message only to reply to you. These exchanges are also subject to the terms of WhatsApp (Meta) or your e-mail provider. I keep them for as long as our conversation needs, and at most three years after the last contact.

5.title: Recipients and transfers
body: Technical and audience data is processed by the host, Vercel Inc., based in the United States. Vercel covers these transfers with standard contractual clauses. No data is sold or used for advertising.

6.title: Retention
body: Your audience measurement choice is kept for 13 months, after which you are asked again. Audience statistics are aggregated and kept according to Vercel's policy.

7.title: Your rights
body: Under applicable data protection law, including the GDPR for visitors from the European Union, you have the right to access, correct, erase, object to and restrict the processing of your data. Write to {{email}}. You may also complain to the data protection authority of your country.
To withdraw your consent to audience measurement, use the "Cookie settings" link at the bottom of every page.
